notes.claim: LSU AgCenter describes reading a pump curve by choosing a flow rate on the horizontal axis, going vertically to the curve, then left to the vertical axis to read the head.
Grundfos says that on a pump's QH-curve a low flow gives a high head and a high flow gives a low head.
LSU AgCenter says the highest head occurs at the lowest flow rate and the highest flow rate occurs at the lowest head.
Mersen shows a curve read the other way round, from a wanted time back to the current that gives it.
Oak National Academy has a learning aim to state the difference between interpolation and extrapolation and the limitations of each.
AQA's Stride guide lists finding values which are not provided on the scales as a foundation skill for graphs.

sources.title: Pump Curves
sources.quote: Choosing a flow rate (for example, 2,000 gallons per minute) on the horizontal axis, proceeding vertically to the pump curve and then proceeding left to the vertical axis, thus reading the head (80 feet).

sources.title: Pump Curves
sources.quote: The highest head occurs at the lowest flow rate, and the highest flow rate occurs at the lowest head.

sources.title: How to read a pump curve? | Grundfos
sources.quote: In a QH-curve, which measures the flow and head, you can see that a low flow results in a high head and a high flow results in a low head.
